text: Fill in the blank: She is ___ honest girl.
explanation: Honest begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so an is used.

text: Fill in the blank: He is the tallest boy ___ the class.
explanation: We say in the class for a group we belong to.

text: Fill in the blank: The meeting is scheduled ___ Monday.
explanation: Days of the week take the preposition on.

text: Fill in the blank: She has been living in this city ___ 2010.
explanation: Since is used with a point in time, such as a year. For is used with a length of time.

text: Fill in the blank: He is very fond ___ music.
explanation: The adjective fond is followed by the preposition of.

text: Fill in the blank: ___ sun rises in the east.
explanation: There is only one sun, so the definite article the is used.

text: Fill in the blank: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
explanation: The verb prefer is followed by to, not than.

text: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He don't / like to / play cricket / in the afternoon.
explanation: With he, the correct form is does not or doesn't, so the first part is wrong.

text: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Each of the / players have / received a / medal.
explanation: Each is singular, so it should be has received, not have.

text: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She did not / went to / school yesterday / due to illness.
explanation: After did not the verb stays in its base form, so it should be go to.

text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence about seniority.
options: She is more senior than me.
explanation: Senior, like junior, is followed by to and not than.

text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence about meeting someone.
options: I am looking forward to meet you.
I am looking forward to meeting you.
I am looking forward for meeting you.
I am looking forward meet you.
explanation: In looking forward to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing: meeting.

text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence about the room.
explanation: Furniture is uncountable. It has no plural form and takes a singular verb.
